title: Two schema sources disagree on whether users.email is unique — a statement valid against one is 42P10 against the other, so a suite can be green on a shape that never runs
description:
**BLUF** — the `users` table has **two schema sources that disagree about whether** `email` **is unique**, and a statement that is valid against one is a hard error against the other. This is not a row-level inconsistency; it is a **test environment diverging from the deployed environment on a constraint**, which means a suite can be green on a shape that never runs anywhere.

## ⛔ DO NOT RECONCILE THESE TWO FILES YET

**Nobody has established which source is authoritative.** Aligning either to the other closes the question by erasing the evidence that it was open — and whichever way it is aligned, the loser's behaviour silently becomes "the contract". Establish authority first, then change one file, deliberately, with the reasoning written down.

## The two sources

| file | declaration |
| -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/docker/init/01-schema.sql:21` | `email TEXT NOT NULL` — **no unique index** |
| `Blockchain/Dev/migrations/001_initial-schema.sql:20` | `email VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL` |

**The first is deliberate and is documented in place.** Its own comment reads: *"email is AES-GCM ciphertext … Lookups go via the deterministic email_lookup_hash … because non-deterministic encryption can't enforce uniqueness."* A unique index on a randomly-IV'd ciphertext cannot block duplicates, so uniqueness was moved to `users_email_lookup_hash_uniq`. `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts` already reflects this — `createUser` conflicts on `email_lookup_hash` and says why.

**So the divergence is probably a migration that was never updated when the encryption landed** — but that is a hypothesis, and this ticket exists so it is checked rather than assumed.

## The evidence, measured

Against the running stack (built from `docker/init/01-schema.sql`), in **rolled-back** transactions:

```
INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (email) DO UPDATE ...
  -> ERROR: there is no unique or exclusion constraint matching
            the ON CONFLICT specification            (42P10)

INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE ...
  -> INSERT 0 1
```

Index census on the live table: `users_pkey (id)`, `users_email_lookup_hash_uniq (email_lookup_hash) WHERE NOT NULL`, and six social-id uniques. **No index on** `email`**.**

## Why this is a class hazard, not one row

**KS-949 F1 is the instance.** The api-gateway startup seed used `ON CONFLICT (email)`. The round-1 QA gate reported *"fresh DB → INSERT 0 12"* — a true measurement, taken against a database built from `migrations/001`. On every environment we actually deploy, the same statement raised 42P10 and the twelve-row seed silently failed on **every** boot, caught and logged at debug level as "skipped".

**A green test against the wrong schema source is indistinguishable from a green test.** That is the hazard: not that one seed was broken, but that the instrument could not tell.

## What "establishing authority" looks like

1. Which source builds which environment today — compose/init vs the migration runner — measured, not assumed.
2. Whether any deployed database was built from `migrations/001` and therefore **does** have the unique index (if so, the same statement behaves differently per environment, which is worse than either alone).
3. Whether `migrations/001` is still executed anywhere, or is now only a historical artefact that tests happen to build from.
4. Only then: change one file, and add a check that the two cannot drift again.

## Scope

**Not** KS-949's (that fixed the instance and is deliberately silent on which source is right). **Not** KS-957's (that is a claims path — artefacts asserting things their suites cannot check; this is a schema-authority question). Filed separately per the aggregation rule: one ticket per logical path.

**Measured 2026-09-07 during KS-949 round 2.**

---

## 🔴 OPEN QUESTION INHERITED BY WHOEVER SETTLES AUTHORITY

**If an environment is built from** `migrations/001`**, does auth's** `seedDemoUsers` **run before document seeding?**

This is a live consequence of the divergence, not a hypothetical, and it is recorded here because it has no other home.

**Why it only exists on one side.** `migrations/001:107` and `deployment/azure/migrate/init.sql:105` declare `documents.owner_user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id)`. `docker/init/01-schema.sql:127` — the deployed source — declares `owner_user_id UUID` with **no** foreign key (verified on the live table via `pg_constraint`; control: that file declares no user foreign keys at all).

**So on a migrations-built database the twelve seeded user rows must exist BEFORE any document referencing them is inserted, and on the deployed schema the question cannot arise.** Same tree, same code, two different ordering requirements.

**Why it is now load-bearing.** KS-949 removes the api-gateway startup migration's user INSERT (ratified 2026-09-07: it has never once succeeded — 42P10 on every boot — and auth's `seedDemoUsers` already creates all twelve rows with identical tenancy, encrypted, with `email_lookup_hash` set). After that change, **auth is the only creator of those rows.** On the deployed schema that is safe. On a migrations-built schema it depends on an ordering nobody has measured.

**What would settle it:** whether any environment is built from `migrations/001` today, and if so, the actual boot order of auth's seeder against whatever inserts documents.

**Deliberately NOT settled here**, and not guessed at. Which source a given environment used is exactly the authority question this ticket exists to answer, and answering the ordering first would be assuming it.

**Raised 2026-09-07 during KS-949 round 2.**

nodes.title: KS-960: pin createUser's conflict target on email_lookup_hash (test only; the reconcile ruling stands)

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Kam ruled the 31-decision card `secuura-backlog-31-decisions-1109` on 2026-11-09 at 13:44:07 (live board), in these words: "Decision secuura-backlog-31-decisions-1109: a — All recommendations (A and B)". Option a reads: "Every row ruled as recommended; a board seat files and moves the tickets; the KS-607 demo rows still wait for a separate yes." This ticket is row A1 of the decision pack, ruled as recommended: option 1. What runs is official: a build seat first reads each environment's schema (read-only), then aligns the other schema files to it and adds a check so they cannot drift apart again. That also fixes the demo-user seed that fails 14 of 14 times (KS-1990).

KS-960 and KS-1200 are one question, and the same ruling is recorded on both. The ticket's "do not reconcile yet" hold stays until that read has been done: the ruling names the authority, and the read comes first. A build seat does the work; nothing was changed in code by this comment.

Alongside this comment the ticket, which was unassigned, is assigned to the board account, and moves from Backlog to Todo.

**BLUF:** The 14-of-14 failure of POST /api/admin/seed-demo-users on a fresh stack (KS-1990) is this ticket's 42P10: the route's INSERT conflicts on `email`, and `users` has no unique index on `email`. Measured on a throwaway local stack at develop 07a2d62be6a0, not on kintsugi or demo. Nothing was changed: no product edit, and neither schema source was touched or reconciled.

- Route: Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts, INSERT at lines 2108-2112, `ON CONFLICT (email) DO NOTHING` at line 2111 (develop 07a2d62be6a0).
- Schema sources at that sha: docker/init/01-schema.sql line 37 `email TEXT NOT NULL`; migrations/001_initial-schema.sql line 20 `email VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL`. No later migration adds a unique constraint on users(email). The compose stack is built from the first, so on that stack the table has no such index.
- Run: disposable compose stack (project w28, images built from develop 07a2d62be6a0, migrations applied=60 failed=0, internal-only network), both demo-seed gate flags set on the originate container only, called as a SYSTEM_ADMIN: HTTP 200, success true, created 0, alreadyPresent 0, failed 14. Controls: a non-admin user gets 403, no token gets 401.
- Originate log: 14 "Demo user seed failed" lines, SQLSTATE 42P10 on 14 of 14, one message: "there is no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification".
- Index census of users on that stack: 14 unique indexes, 0 of them on email. The only email indexes are a non-unique one on lower(email) and the unique partial index users_email_lookup_hash_uniq on email_lookup_hash.
- Changed-input proof, each statement in its own rolled-back transaction, run as the application role with the platform-scope setting the route uses: the route's statement for the first user with ON CONFLICT (email) gives ERROR 42P10; the same statement with no ON CONFLICT clause gives INSERT 0 1; with ON CONFLICT (id) it gives INSERT 0 1; all 14 rows with no ON CONFLICT clause give INSERT 0 1 on 14 of 14, so no second cause sits behind the 42P10. Rows for the 14 seed ids: 0 before, 0 after.
- Not measured: kintsugi and demo; any schema other than the compose init schema; what a fix should look like (the ticket's own warning against reconciling the two sources stands).

## BLUF
The owed pin **merged**: PR #1000, squash `4ec051032fdab1bfc82854c77273735dc0b8af8c` on develop (parent `0b25f823f`). Nothing is deployed. **This ticket stays open.** The DO NOT RECONCILE ruling stands, and which schema source is authoritative is still undecided.

## Recommendation
No action needed on the pin. The reconciliation decision is still owed separately.

## Detail
- Merge verified at origin: develop tip = the merge commit, single parent `0b25f823f`, 1 file, blob identical to the gated head `ab4a35d75`.
- Tier-2 QA gate: GO WITH FINDINGS at `ab4a35d75`. Its Polish note (cell 3 is whitespace-brittle, cell 2 case-blind with cell 1 backing it) is left as a possible follow-up, not changed on this head.
- Board: opening the PR walked this ticket Backlog → In Progress (GitHub integration). It is set back to **Backlog**, its state before the PR, because the ticket's main ask has not started. The PR description was re-worded before the merge so Linear linked it as "contributes", not "closes"; it did not walk to Done.

## BLUF
PR #1000 raises the owed PIN at head `ab4a35d75d9b7611b4588ce88a792a489a124324`, not yet merged. One auth test asserts `createUser` conflicts on `email_lookup_hash` and never on `email`. **This ticket stays open:** the "⛔ DO NOT RECONCILE THESE TWO FILES YET" ruling is untouched, and which schema source is authoritative is still undecided.

## Recommendation
No action needed on the PR. The reconciliation decision is still owed separately.

## Detail
- PR: https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1000 (branch `feature/ks-960-ornith-createuser-conflict-target-pin`, base develop `0b25f823f`).
- Authored by the local model (Ornith) from a Wednesday-written brief; source-read by Wednesday; re-run by seat A at `ab4a35d75d9b7611b4588ce88a792a489a124324`.
- Red-proof: `userRepo.ts:688` narrowed to `ON CONFLICT (email) DO UPDATE SET` reddens exactly cells 1–3. Dropping only the partial-index predicate reddens exactly cell 3. Both controls and the completeness cell stay green, with 6 cells ran in every row.
- auth 60 files / 740 tests pass (baseline 59 / 734, 0 pre-existing failures measured at `0b25f823f`). `tsc` rc 0.
- Neither `docker/init/01-schema.sql` nor `migrations/001_initial-schema.sql` is touched.

**The third column is now MEASURED on the deployed database, not inferred. Still NOT reconciled.**

This ticket already records `documents.issuer_organization_id` as a third instance of the divergence: `migrations/001_initial-schema.sql:105` declares it `REFERENCES organizations(id)`, `docker/init/01-schema.sql:125` declares it with no reference. That was read from the two files.

Read-only, from the database the demo actually runs (2026-09-07, during deploy verification):

```
FK constraints naming issuer_organization_id : 0
```

Controls on the same connection: `users` reports 33 columns; `uuid_generate_v4` present in `pg_proc`.

**So for this column the deployed schema is `docker/init`, measured.** That is one more data point for whichever source turns out to be authoritative — and it is one column, not a general answer. **The ruling stands: do not reconcile these files until authority is established.**

Also recorded on KS-597 (#889), where it changes how the resolution subquery should be read.

**A THIRD column shows the same divergence — found while opening #889 (KS-597). Recorded, NOT reconciled.**

`documents.issuer_organization_id`:
- `migrations/001_initial-schema.sql:105` — `issuer_organization_id UUID REFERENCES organizations(id)` — **with** a foreign key.
- `docker/init/01-schema.sql:125` — `issuer_organization_id UUID` — **without** one.

The running DB was measured (by the KS-597 author, on the live DB) to have **no** FK on this column — so the deployed schema matches `docker/init`, not `migrations/001`. Same direction as this ticket's other two instances.

**Why it is not cosmetic:** KS-597's resolution subquery folds an unknown or cross-tenant org id to NULL specifically because there is no FK to reject it. On the schema `migrations/001` describes, the database would refuse a dangling reference by itself; on the schema we deploy, nothing does. A reader reconciling these two files in the wrong direction would therefore also change whether that code is load-bearing.

**Not reconciled here, per this ticket's ruling** — authority between the two sources has to be established first.

## A SECOND column, so the divergence is a PATTERN rather than one row

Found while settling an unrelated question (KS-949's fresh-database case). The two sources disagree about `documents.owner_user_id` in exactly the same way they disagree about `users.email`:

| file | declaration |
| --- | --- |
| `docker/init/01-schema.sql:127` — **the deployed source** | `owner_user_id UUID` — **no foreign key** |
| `migrations/001_initial-schema.sql:107` | `owner_user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id)` |
| `deployment/azure/migrate/init.sql:105` | `owner_user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id)` |

Confirmed on the live local table: `pg_constraint` reports **no** FK from `documents.owner_user_id` to `users`, against 59 documents that have the column set.

**Control:** the same search for `REFERENCES users` across `docker/init/01-schema.sql` returns **nothing at all** — so that file does not merely omit this one FK, it declares no user foreign keys. The grep can find `REFERENCES` elsewhere in the tree, so the empty result is a real absence.

## Why this matters more than an extra example

`services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts` justifies its twelve-row user seed as *"seed per-client users into the main (default tenant) DB so document FK constraints work"*.

**That justification is true on one schema source and false on the other.** On a database built from `migrations/001` the FK exists and the ordering matters; on the database we actually deploy there is no constraint to satisfy. **A comment explaining why code exists can be correct and misleading at the same time, depending on which source built the database it runs against** — and nothing in the tree tells a reader which one they are on.

That is the class hazard this ticket describes, and it is now measured twice. The first instance (`users.email`) made a statement invalid; this one makes a *rationale* unverifiable. **Both point at the same missing fact: which source is authoritative.**

Still: **do not reconcile.** Two data points make the question more urgent, not more obvious.

**Measured 2026-09-07.**
